answer: Tie each agent identity to a verifiable work history and a small refundable stake that acts as an anchor, so creating a new identity is cheap but earning trust is not. In the reputation graph, each verified interaction adds a weighted edge, and a vertex with many independent, long-lived neighbours counts far more than a cluster of fresh accounts vouching for each other. A mirror check then compares claimed history against public attestations, so copied or circular endorsements lose weight instead of multiplying influence.
